summary: Reverified only s1_cluster_size_cv_low_agency_vs_control, s1_noise_ratio_low_agency_vs_control, and s1_unique_clusters_low_agency_vs_control. Read the complete 42-page paper markdown, including references and Appendices A and B, and independently extracted the cited PDF page and relevant methods, figures, and appendices with pymupdf. PDF p. 17 confirms unique-cluster difference/test statistic 3.33 with p = .04, noise-ratio difference/test statistic 0.22 with p = .02, and cluster-size-CV difference/test statistic 0.75 with p = .005. The paper describes maximum-minus-minimum condition-mean permutation tests and identifies Control above Low-Agency for unique clusters and noise ratio, and Low-Agency above Control for CV. The recorded orientations and notes correctly preserve that these are extreme-condition comparisons, not separately reported fixed-pair tests. Analyzed participant counts, analyzed-set counts, arm means, SDs, SEs, and numerical confidence limits for these analyses are not printed; null entries are appropriate. The recruitment count on PDF pp. 10 and 14 precedes the exclusions described on pp. 13-14 and must not be substituted or reduced by calculation. The requested coding fields are supported: across_people, diversity, category_count, set, immediate, outcome_with_ai = true, within_person = null, and ai_vs_bau. Higher unique-cluster counts and noise ratios mean more_diverse; higher cluster-size CV means more_similar under the authors' interpretation (PDF pp. 16-18 and 32). All three reported script flags are false positives under the supplied rules: extraction-spec.md explicitly permits se_basis = unclear in its JSON structure and Field notes, and creativity-codebook.md section 10 defines unclear for a printed test whose unit of analysis the paper does not establish. PDF p. 17 reports permutation tests but does not identify what is permuted or treated as independent; Figure 3 on p. 32 establishes the condition-object set used to compute the metric, not the uncertainty unit. Neither appendix supplies the missing resampling detail. Retain unclear for all three estimates. Coverage review under extraction rules 4-6 found no missing eligible reported outcome or contrast. The qualitative High-Agency versus Low-Agency CV comparison on p. 18 is already represented; self-reports, chat-process measures, and participant-AI overlap are appropriately excluded.
